skills.name: Practical preparation: reading a bar chart

note.text: A bar chart compares separate categories using bars of equal width and a common scale. Leave gaps between categories. The height measures the value, not the width or colour. Start a simple frequency bar chart at zero to make length comparisons fair. Always label the measured unit. In this guided practical, use the chart on screen, read the values and check them against a table in your exercise book.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: A bar chart compares separate categories using bars of equal width and a common scale. Leave gaps between categories. The height measures the value, not the width or colour. Start a simple frequency bar chart at zero to make length comparisons fair. Always label the measured unit. In this guided practical, use the chart on screen, read the values and check them against a table in your exercise book.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: The chart compares basket sales by Bih, Ayuk and Ngozi. The names are categories; the vertical values count baskets. Read each bar from the same baseline. Record name and quantity in a small table, then compare the largest and smallest values. These are invented classroom data, not a survey of actual traders.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Write a title, category labels and the baskets unit. Plot equal-width bars at a consistent scale. To check a drawing, reread each height and compare it with the original data. A taller bar represents more baskets in this chart, not automatically a higher price or profit.

key_words.meaning: the value read against the common scale
the common starting line for the bars
the number of occurrences or items counted

examples: The chart has separate bars for named traders.
Bih's bar reaches a marked baskets value.
Each bar starts at the same zero line.

mistake.wrong: The width of a category bar is the trader's profit.
mistake.right: category: a separate group being compared.
mistake.why: Categories identify groups; heights show the measured quantity.
